newsitem.title: USA: Merck second-quarter results beat expectations.
newsitem.headline: Merck second-quarter results beat expectations.

text.p: Merck & Co. said Thursday its second-quarter earnings rose 19 percent, slightly above Wall Street expectations, as demand continued to grow for its major pharmaceutical products.
Separately, Merck and Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc. said they plan to close the merger of their animal health and poultry genetics businesses on July 31.

The 50-50 joint venture, Merial Ltd., will be the world's largest company solely dedicated to the discovery, manufacture and marketing of veterinary pharmaceuticals and vaccines, with a revenue base of $1.9 billion and more than 6,000 employees worldwide. Merial is expected to become operational on Aug. 1.
Merck said its earnings rose to $1.15 billion from $972.1 million in the year-ago period. Sales jumped 20 percent to $5.9 billion from almost $5 billion.
Whitehouse Station, N.J.-based Merck's stock surged $7 to $105.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
For the six months ended June 30, profits climbed 18 percent to 2.2 billion from $1.8 billion. Sales grew 22 percent to $11.5 billion from $9.4 billion.

"Sales growth for the quarter and the first half of 1997 continued to be led by established major products, recent product introductions and the Merck-Medco Managed Care business," said Raymond Gilmartin, chairman, in a statement.
"Both our domestic and international operations reported strong unit volume gains."

Foreign exchange fluctuations reduced second-quarter sales growth by 1 percentage point, Merck said. Excluding this effect, sales of Merck human and animal health products grew 15 percent for the quarter.

"Income growth for the first six months was driven by strong unit volume gains," Gilmartin said. "The unfavourable effects of inflation, net of price, and exchange were partially offset by cost controls and productivity improvements in manufacturing, selling and general and administrative expenses."
